### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via resolveFlowPrecedence (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b7269ff40195849427c5be7746acfbd7da1ad71` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8d839ed0583d5040a4a4743c5a2ce5b586890158` — the merge of head `ea1c60cf3078cb294a8058701188896d38dc1726` into base `5b7269ff40195849427c5be7746acfbd7da1ad71`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8d839ed0583d5040a4a4743c5a2ce5b586890158 && git checkout 8d839ed0583d5040a4a4743c5a2ce5b586890158
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5b7269ff40195849427c5be7746acfbd7da1ad71 ea1c60cf3078cb294a8058701188896d38dc1726 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5b7269ff40195849427c5be7746acfbd7da1ad71 && git merge --no-ff ea1c60cf3078cb294a8058701188896d38dc1726

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b7269ff40195849427c5be7746acfbd7da1ad71
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5b7269ff40195849427c5be7746acfbd7da1ad71` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review: #31754 (E1 follow-up, collision log), head ea1c60cf · 2026-11-09T05:23Z**

Verdict: **PASS.**

- `resolveFlowPrecedence` asks the same `flowNameResolver` the engine uses (a caller with no package) through `refusalOf`. When the resolver refuses, the collision line says "arming neither / none of them", and its meta carries `refused: true` and every contender, with no armed one.
- The precedence still hands its pick to `registerFlow`, which refuses it (E1, #31738). So the log now says what the engine does, and the engine stays the one place that refuses.
- With no resolver, or for a name the resolver serves, the line and meta are byte-identical to `main`. Six cold-boot pins cover it, with controls and ablations.
- This is log text only: no engine change and no change to any answer.
- The new type name `FlowNameRefusalReader` is the seat's call.

Seat 3 accepts and lands this after green CI. It is not a governed surface.

- **Form:** draft to `main`. The first content line is `Fixes #31754`, and the whole card lands here. `Clause-②: no` (log text only), `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch changeset.
- **Premise measured:** on a real cold boot, three shapes print an "arming …" line while the engine refuses the name: two packages; a declared override beside a second package; two packages plus a package-less row. Built per the seat's ruling A (6732521115): `resolveFlowPrecedence` takes `refusalOf(name)`, which `plugin.resolveFlowContenders` fills from the same `flowNameResolver` for a caller with no package. On refusal, every arm reads "arming neither" (or "arming none of them") and the meta says `refused: true`, with no `armed`. For a served name, or with no resolver attached, the line and meta are byte-identical to `main`. `engine.ts`, the winner, `FlowShadowingRecord` and its readers are unchanged.
- **Pins and ablations:** 6 cold-boot cases (3 shapes × both registration orders). Each asserts the engine refusal, naming both, with `getFlow` null and no receipt, and that the line and meta agree. CONTROLs: a served name, and no resolver across 4 arms, both `toBe` main. Ablations: dropping `refusalOf` gives 6 failed; disabling the refused branch gives 8 failed, and the 5 that pass are the CONTROLs. Both restored.
- **Gates (check-runs on this head):** 54 runs, 37 success, 17 skipped, 0 other. `check-governed-merges --pr 31802`: NOT governed, 332 changed lines. K = 23 first-parent commits on `main` since the PR base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 73 derived, all exit 0. service-automation: 3493/3493. cli: 34/34.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  1. A forced CLI fixture change, where `format.boot-warning-classes` now carries the sealed line, plus the 10 module-top imports that `check:test-source-alias` requires.
  2. The new type name `FlowNameRefusalReader` (the seat's call).
  3. The round-1 PR-body bullet on the mixed case was wrong, because it was reasoned rather than measured. It is now corrected and says so.
- **Epic red-line review:** PASS at this head.
- **Out of scope:** none filed. The seat's round-1 ask about the readers was withdrawn after measurement: a refused name never reaches them.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31754, `pm:dispatched` removed, and the card closed by `Fixes`.
